title: Provider auth a gatekeeper would accept: a federation or regulator CA, tested at the edges
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22, hard blocker.

Three mechanisms exist (epic mimid-75nk): RFC 9421 DNS keys, DANE, and
PKIX from configured anchors. But AGENTS.md is explicit that mutually
authenticated TLS has never been completed with a NON-MIMID peer, and
says mimid must not claim conformance to protocol-07 §4.1 without
Mark's OK.

A mandated regime almost certainly means a regulator or federation CA.
That is `pkix_anchors` shaped, and it is the mechanism least tested at
its edges. What "the edges" means concretely, and none of it is
exercised today:

- intermediates. A federation CA will not issue leaves from its root.
  Note tls.rs's own Limitation: through a reverse proxy only the LEAF
  certificate arrives, so intermediates must be in mimid's trust
  configuration rather than arriving in the handshake. mimi.reviewcommit.com
  is deployed exactly that way (Caddy on joumon), so this is live, not
  theoretical.
- revocation. No CRL, no OCSP, no story. Against a friendly peer this
  never comes up; under a mandate, a revoked gatekeeper certificate that
  mimid keeps accepting is a compliance failure.
- name constraints and path length, policy OIDs, and whatever else a
  regulator's CA puts in its certificates.
- cross-signing and CA rotation, which a long-lived federation will do.

WHY mimid-75nk.12 STOPS BEING A NICETY HERE, in Mark's words: "against
a peer with no incentive to help you debug, a bare 403 is the difference
between an afternoon and a quarter." That bead is now CLOSED, implemented
this session: a 403 carries a `reason` naming the source provider's own
DNS record, signature or certificate, while saying nothing about our
trust list. The value of that lands here.

Related and unfinished: mimid-6x2f (mTLS tested with a real peer, both
halves, and an interop-day test plan) is the concrete next step and was
promised to Rohan Mahy and Konrad Kohbrok in Mark's email of 2026-11-18.
